newsitem.title: New zealand: NZ dollar ends easier, upside risk intact.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends easier, upside risk intact.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed easier on Tuesday but dealers said its upside risk remained intact.
"I think there's still a possibility we will have a look higher in the Kiwi, maybe not today, but certainly towards the week's close," said a chief bank dealer.
"I think we're going to have a test of somewhere closer towards US$0.6975 before we see the Kiwi come lower."
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6931/38 and at 68.99 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6948/55 at 69.13 at the open.
"We saw some offshore selling first up, and that really caught the market a little bit long," the senior dealer added.

Dealers said kiwi/samurai and euro bond issuance had pushed the Kiwi higher on Monday but activity had subsided on Tuesday. "There's still reasonable interest around in that investor market, although obviously they're not coming thick and fast," one said.
Short term, the risk for the Kiwi remained on the upside.

"I don't believe the Kiwi is going to sustain these levels further out, but short term there's a risk we might have another look higher, particularly if the Aussie continues higher," the chief dealer said.
